shared.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
shared.description:
Aboriginal Peoples are the Traditional custodians of Australia and are represented by more than 250 language groups, each connected with a particular Country. Torres Strait Islander Peoples are represented by 5 major island groups and are connected with islands to the north of Australia’s Cape York which were annexed by Queensland in 1879. 

An Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person is someone who: 

  • is of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent 
  • identifies as an Aboriginal person and/or Torres Strait Islander person, and 
  • is accepted as such by the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Community(ies) in which they live.

shared.title: Aboriginal English
shared.description: A recognised dialect of English which is the first, or home language, of many Aboriginal people. It differs from other dialects of English, such as Standard Australian English, in systematic ways including sounds, grammar, words and their meanings, and language use. Aboriginal English is a powerful vehicle for the expression of Aboriginal identity. Aboriginal English is not a target language study option for NSW Aboriginal Languages syllabuses.

shared.title: Aboriginal Songline(s)
shared.description: Texts that describe landscapes and directions of the tracks forged in lands, waters and skies by Creator Spirits during the Dreaming.

shared.title: accessibility
shared.description: The extent to which a system, environment or object may be used irrespective of a user’s capabilities or abilities. For example, the use of assistive technologies (AT) to allow people with disability to use computer systems, or the use of icons in place of words to allow young children to use a system.

shared.title: assistive technology (AT)
shared.description: A device or system whose primary purpose is to maintain or improve an individual's functioning and independence to facilitate participation and enhance overall wellbeing. This includes technologies specifically designed to meet an individual's needs, eg eye gaze technology, as well as more general technologies that can be used by anyone, eg speech-to-text applications. Assistive technology can also be referred to as inclusive technology.

shared.title: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
shared.description:
An umbrella term that encompasses the communication methods used to supplement or replace speech or writing. AAC can be unaided, such as gestures, body language and sign language, or aided such as pictures, symbols, objects or speech generating devices.

See communication systems

shared.title: communication forms
shared.description: The ways people communicate and the communicative behaviours they use. Communication forms can be non-symbolic and/or symbolic. Non-symbolic forms include sounds, gestures, facial expressions and eye movements. Symbolic forms can be aided or non-aided. Aided forms of symbolic communication include objects, symbols, photographs and drawings. Aided forms can be digital. Non-aided forms of symbolic communication include formal gestures; speech; and signs, such as Key Word Sign.

shared.title: copyright
shared.description: The protection provided to the creators of original works and makers of sound recordings and films, that offers a legal framework for the control and reproduction or transmission of their literary, dramatic, artistic or musical works.

shared.title: Country/Place
shared.description:
Country is used to describe a specific area of a nation or clan including physical, linguistic and spiritual features. Aboriginal communities’ cultural associations with their Country may include or relate to languages, cultural practices, knowledge, songs, stories, art, paths, landforms, flora, fauna and minerals. These cultural associations may include custodial relationships with particular landscapes such as land, sea, sky, rivers as well as the intangible places associated with the Dreaming(s). Custodial relationships are extremely important in determining who may have the capacity to authentically speak for their Country. 

Place is a space mapped out by physical or intangible boundaries that individuals or groups of Torres Strait Islander Peoples occupy and regard as their own. It is a space with varying degrees of spirituality.

shared.title: culture
shared.description: The customs, habits, beliefs/spirituality, social organisation and ways of life that characterise different groups and communities. Cultural characteristics give a group or individual a sense of who they are and help them make sense of the world in which they live. Culture is a shared system but inherently diverse – there can be individual and group differences within cultures. Everyone has culture – it is a lens through which we see the world.

shared.title: custodians
shared.description: In Aboriginal communities, an individual charged with maintaining and passing on particular elements of cultural significance, eg language, stories, songs, rituals and imagery.

shared.title: d/Deaf
shared.description: When referring to deaf people who belong to a linguistic and cultural minority known as the Deaf community, the 'D' may be capitalised in reference to the individual, the group, or the culture in order to accord respect and deference, for example, the Deaf community. When referring simply to audiological status or when cultural affiliation is not known, as in the case of a person with a hearing loss in general, the lowercase 'd', as in 'deaf' is the more common usage.

shared.title: Deaf
shared.description: A cultural identity for people with hearing loss who share a common culture and who usually have a shared sign language.

shared.title: disability
shared.description:
An umbrella term for any or all of the following components: 

  • impairments: challenges in body function or structure
  • activity limitations: difficulties in executing activities
  • participation restrictions: challenges an individual may experience in involvement in life situations. (World Health Organization)

shared.title: diversity
shared.description: Differences that exist within a group, for example, age, sex, gender, gender expression, sexuality, ethnicity, ability/disability, body shape and composition, culture, religion/spirituality, learning differences, socioeconomic background, values and experiences.

shared.title: Dreaming
shared.description: The Dreaming has different meanings for different Aboriginal groups. The Dreaming can be seen as the embodiment of Aboriginal creation which gives meaning to everything; the essence of Aboriginal beliefs about creation and spiritual and physical existence. It establishes the rules governing relationships between the people, the land and all things for Aboriginal Peoples. The Dreaming is linked to the past, the present and the future. Where appropriate, refer to Aboriginal names for the Dreaming.

shared.title: Elders
shared.description: The custodians of knowledge and lore. They are chosen and accepted by their own communities as people who have the permission to disclose cultural knowledge and beliefs. Recognised Elders are highly respected people within Aboriginal communities. Proper consultation with local Aboriginal communities will often direct schools to recognised Elders.

shared.title: first language(s)
shared.description: The first language(s) that a person learns to speak.

shared.title: Indigenous
shared.description:
An internationally recognised term for the first peoples of a land. In NSW the term Aboriginal person/Peoples is preferred.

See Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

shared.title: Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP)
shared.description:
Includes, but is not limited to, objects, sites, cultural knowledge, cultural expression and the arts, that have been transmitted or continue to be transmitted through generations as belonging to a particular Indigenous group or Indigenous people as a whole or their territory. 

See intellectual property

shared.title: intellectual property
shared.description:
Non-material assets such as forms of cultural expression that belong to a particular individual or community. Intellectual property rights refer to the rights that the law grants to individuals for the protection of creative, intellectual, scientific and industrial activity, such as inventions. 

See Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP), and copyright

shared.title: Key Word Sign
shared.description: A communication strategy that incorporates signing with speech. It is used to support language development for people with communication difficulties. Although Key Word Sign uses a simplified form of manual signing, it is different to Auslan, as it is not a signed language.

shared.title: kinship
shared.description: A key aspect of Aboriginal cultures and values. It includes the importance of all relationships and of being related to and belonging to the land.

shared.title: language group
shared.description: An Aboriginal community identified with a common language, both verbal and nonverbal, and with a particular territory. Used in preference to the term ‘tribe’.

shared.title: language revival
shared.description: The process and range of strategies for increasing knowledge and use of a language that is no longer spoken fluently across all generations in the context of language loss or language dispossession caused by colonisation. Aboriginal Languages and Torres Strait Islander Languages are being revived through community initiatives, linguistic research and school programs. ‘Language revival’ may be used as an overarching term that could also include ‘reclamation’, ‘revitalisation’, ‘renewal’ and ‘reawakening’.

shared.title: local Aboriginal community
shared.description:
A local Aboriginal community is constituted by those people who are Aboriginal and who reside in the near locality. Aboriginal communities will have a rich and diverse history that has been seriously affected by dispossession and relations, which sees families with spiritual connection to Country residing beside those who have been forced to move from other locations. The notion of locality is complex and multilayered: schools should seek advice from a range of people and/or organisations representing local interests. 

See community(ies)

shared.title: off-Country
shared.description:
Taking place away from Aboriginal land or Country of origin. 

See Country/Place

shared.title: on-Country
shared.description:
Taking place on Aboriginal land or Country of origin.

See Country/Place

shared.title: protocols
shared.description: The appropriate ways of behaving, communicating and showing respect for diversity of history and culture. This involves appreciation of the knowledge, standing and status of people within the local Aboriginal community and the school community. Protocols inevitably vary between communities, and between people within a community. In establishing a partnership between schools and Aboriginal communities, it is especially important that protocols are acknowledged and respected.

shared.title: sign
shared.description: Hand signs (or hand talk) used to supplement or replace oral language. Signs form part of nonverbal communication for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and may be used by people who are hearing, or d/Deaf or hard of hearing. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Sign Languages may be used in some areas. Some Sign Languages may be associated with sacred ceremonial practices.

shared.title: signage
shared.description: The use of words, graphic designs and/or symbols used to communicate a message, eg information signs, plaques, warning signs, road signs, signs that show direction.

shared.title: switch
shared.description:
A type of assistive technology that enables people with cognitive and/or physical disability to access a range of devices, including computers and communication devices. Switches can be activated by touch, or triggered without contact, such as through eye gaze, sound or blowing.

See assistive technology (AT)

shared.title: yarning circle
shared.description: Yarning circles are an important cultural practice for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples to learn within the collective group. Knowledge and information are shared in harmony and respect with all individuals.

specific.title: accuracy
specific.description: The extent to which measurements are considered to be close to the true value.

specific.title: alpha (decay)
specific.description: Radioactive disintegration in which positively charged particles composed of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (and therefore equivalent to the nucleus of a helium atom) are emitted.

specific.title: antinode
specific.description: A point in a standing wave where the amplitude of oscillation is at its maximum, which occurs halfway between 2 nodes.

specific.title: area vector (normal)
specific.description: A vector that is perpendicular to a surface and whose magnitude equals the area of that surface. It’s used to calculate electric flux or magnetic flux through a surface.

specific.title: attraction (electrical)
specific.description: The force that pulls opposite electric charges toward each other.

specific.title: back emf (back electromotive force)
specific.description: The voltage that is induced in a motor's coil when the motor is running. It opposes the applied voltage and is a direct consequence of the Law of Electromagnetic Induction.

specific.title: baryon
specific.description: A type of subatomic particle made up of 3 quarks and are part of the hadron family – particles that experience the strong nuclear force.

specific.title: beta (decay)
specific.description: A radioactive transformation in which high-energy, high-speed electrons are emitted.

specific.title: beta-minus decay
specific.description: A type of radioactive decay in which a neutron inside an unstable atomic nucleus transforms into a proton and, in the process, emits a beta particle (which is an electron) and an electron antineutrino.

specific.title: beta-plus transformation
specific.description: A type of radioactive decay where a proton in an unstable nucleus is transformed into a neutron and emits a positron and an electron neutrino.

specific.title: binding energy
specific.description: The energy required to split a nucleus of an atom into its individual protons and neutrons.

specific.title: black body (ideal)
specific.description: An object that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation, regardless of wavelength or angle, and emits radiation with a characteristic spectrum that depends only on its temperature, not its material or surface.

specific.title: blueshift
specific.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to shorter (bluer) wavelengths, indicating it is moving toward the observer.

specific.title: boson
specific.description: A type of fundamental particle that carries forces in nature.

specific.title: cathode ray
specific.description: A stream of electrons observed in vacuum tubes which are emitted from the cathode (the negatively charged electrode) and travel toward the anode (the positively charged electrode).

specific.title: centripetal acceleration
specific.description: The acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path that keeps an object moving in a uniform circular motion.

specific.title: centripetal force
specific.description: The net force that acts toward the centre of a circular path, causing an object to move in uniform circular motion.

specific.title: conservative forces
specific.description: Forces where work done on an object depends only on initial and final positions, not the path taken.

specific.title: constructive interference
specific.description: Occurs when 2 or more waves combine in phase, causing their amplitudes to add together to produce a wave with a larger amplitude than the original waves.

specific.title: controlled variable
specific.description: A variable that is kept constant (or changed in constant ways) during an investigation. For example, the same amount of water would be a controlled variable in an investigation comparing solubility.

specific.title: conventional current
specific.description: The flow of positive charge from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a power source in a circuit.

specific.title: decay constant
specific.description: Represents the probability per unit time in which a given nucleus will decay.

specific.title: dependent variable
specific.description: The factor in an experiment that changes in response to changes to the independent variable.

specific.title: destructive interference
specific.description: Occurs when the crests and troughs of 2 interfering waves of equal frequency and opposite phase meet, and their amplitudes cancel out.

specific.title: diffraction
specific.description: The bending and spreading of waves when they encounter an obstacle or pass through a narrow opening.

specific.title: elastic collision
specific.description: A type of collision where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

specific.title: electric circuit
specific.description: A closed path through which electric current flows. It typically consists of a power source, conductive wires, and electrical components.

specific.title: electric permittivity
specific.description: A measure of how much resistance is encountered when forming an electric field in a medium.

specific.title: electric potential energy
specific.description: The energy in charged objects as a result of their position in an electric field.

specific.title: electromagnetic induction
specific.description: The production of an electromotive force (emf) across an electrical conductor in a changing magnetic field.

specific.title: electromagnetic spectrum
specific.description: The complete range of electromagnetic waves arranged by frequency or wavelength, spanning from low-frequency radio waves to high-frequency gamma rays.

specific.title: electromotive force (emf)
specific.description: The energy supplied per unit charge by an energy source such as an electric generator or a battery.

specific.title: equipotential
specific.description: Refers to a region in an electric or gravitational field where the potential is the same at every point, meaning that no work is done when moving a charge or mass along an equipotential.

specific.title: experimental control
specific.description:
The sample in an experiment to which all the other samples are compared.

Extended in Science 11–12: The sample in an experiment that does not receive the independent variable.

specific.title: force
specific.description: A push or pull between objects, which may cause one or both objects to change speed, and/or direction of their motion, and/or their shape.

specific.title: frequency shift phenomenon
specific.description: The observed change in the frequency of a wave when there is relative motion between the source and the observer.

specific.title: friction
specific.description: The resistance to motion that occurs when 2 surfaces rub against each other.

specific.title: fusion (nuclear)
specific.description: A process in which 2 or more atomic nuclei combine to form a single, heavier nucleus, releasing a large amount of energy in the process.

specific.title: geostationary orbit
specific.description: A geosynchronous orbit of a satellite where a satellite orbits directly above the equator in the same direction as Earth’s rotation and has an orbital period equal to Earth’s period of rotation.

specific.title: gravitational potential energy
specific.description: The energy possessed by a mass due to its position in a gravitational field.

specific.title: half-life
specific.description: The time it takes for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

specific.title: hazard
specific.description: A source that poses a potential risk of harm or injury.

specific.title: independent variable
specific.description: The variable that is deliberately changed, often through a series of pre-set values.

specific.title: inelastic collision
specific.description: A type of collision where momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not, as some of the kinetic energy is converted into other forms of energy.

specific.title: inertial frame of reference
specific.description: A viewpoint in which Newton’s First Law (the law of inertia) holds true.

specific.title: inverse square law
specific.description: A physical quantity, like light, sound, or gravity, that diminishes in intensity in proportion to the square of the distance from its source, so doubling the distance reduces the intensity to one-fourth.

specific.title: length contraction
specific.description: A relativistic phenomenon where an object moving at a high velocity appears shorter along the direction of motion to a stationary observer.

specific.title: lepton
specific.description: A type of fundamental particle that does not experience the strong nuclear force.

specific.title: longitudinal (wave)
specific.description: A type of wave in which the disturbance or oscillation of the medium occurs in the same direction as the direction of propagation of the wave.

specific.title: magnetic permeability
specific.description: A measure of how readily a material can support the formation of a magnetic field within itself when exposed to an external magnetic field.

specific.title: mass defect
specific.description: The difference between the total mass of the individual nucleons in a nucleus and the actual mass of the nucleus itself.

specific.title: mean
specific.description: The sum of values in a dataset divided by the total number of values in the dataset. Also called the average.

specific.title: mechanical energy
specific.description: Is the energy of an object due to its kinetic energy and potential energy.

specific.title: mechanical wave
specific.description: A type of wave that requires a medium, such as air, water or a solid material, to travel through.

specific.title: model
specific.description: A mathematical, conceptual or physical representation that describes, simplifies, clarifies or provides an explanation of the structure, workings or relationships within an object, system or idea. Models can provide a means of testing and predicting behaviour within limited conditions. Models may be physical or exist in digital form.

specific.title: monochromatic light
specific.description: Light that consists of a single wavelength or frequency – meaning it is pure light of one colour of one specific energy.

specific.title: muon
specific.description: Part of the lepton group which are a type of fundamental particle.

specific.title: node
specific.description: A point along a standing wave in a vibrating medium where the amplitude is always zero meaning no movement occurs at that position.

specific.title: non-conservative forces
specific.description: Forces that dissipate mechanical energy from a system, usually by converting it into other forms like heat, sound or deformation; the work done by non-conservative forces depends on the path taken.

specific.title: non-inertial frame of reference
specific.description: A viewpoint that is accelerating relative to an inertial frame and to which Newton’s laws of motion do not apply directly.

specific.title: nucleosynthesis
specific.description: The process by which new atomic nuclei are formed from pre-existing protons and neutrons.

specific.title: orbital velocity
specific.description: The velocity at which a satellite must travel to maintain a particular orbit at a given altitude under the influence of gravity alone.

specific.title: outlier
specific.description: A data value that appears to stand out from the other members of the dataset by being unusually high or low.

specific.title: pattern
specific.description: A pattern is made up of a number of elements that repeat or follow a rule.

specific.title: percentage error
specific.description: The absolute error of a measurement expressed as a percentage of the recorded measurement.

specific.title: photoelectric effect
specific.description: The process in which a photon ejects an electron from an atom so that all the energy of the photon is absorbed in separating the electron and imparting kinetic energy to it.

specific.title: photoelectron
specific.description: An electron that is ejected from a material, usually a metal, when it absorbs energy from incident light (photons) as a result of the photoelectric effect.

specific.title: photon
specific.description: A massless, chargeless particle that represents a quantum with its energy being proportional to the frequency of the radiation.

specific.title: potential energy
specific.description: The energy that an object possesses due to its position in a force field or that is stored in a system by virtue of the configuration and interaction between bodies in that system, e.g. elastic potential energy.

specific.title: precision
specific.description: The extent to which repeated measurements of the same item are close to each other.

specific.title: prediction
specific.description: A statement or estimate about what will happen in the future, often based on available evidence, past experiences or statistical analysis.

specific.title: qualitative
specific.description: To use descriptive explanations involving features, characteristics or properties to identify important components. Data and information that is not numerical in nature.

specific.title: quantised energy
specific.description: The concept that energy in a physical system can only exist in discrete, fixed amounts, rather than any arbitrary value.

specific.title: quantitative
specific.description: Data or components that can be expressed or measured numerically, including chemical formulae or numbers.

specific.title: quark
specific.description: A fundamental subatomic particle that experiences all 4 fundamental forces (including the strong nuclear force) and combines to form hadrons.

specific.title: radioactivity
specific.description: The spontaneous emission of particles or energy from the unstable nucleus of certain atoms as they decay into more stable forms.

specific.title: range (of a dataset)
specific.description: The difference between the highest and lowest values in a dataset.

specific.title: rarefactions
specific.description: Regions in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are spread apart, resulting in decreased density and pressure compared to the surrounding areas.

specific.title: redshift
specific.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to longer (redder) wavelengths, indicating it is moving away from the observer.

specific.title: reflection
specific.description: The changed direction of a wave when it bounces off a surface.

specific.title: refraction
specific.description: The changed direction (bending) of a wave when it passes through one transparent substance into another.

specific.title: relativistic momentum
specific.description: The momentum of an object moving close to the speed of light, where classical momentum formulas no longer apply: momentum increases more rapidly than classical momentum as an object’s speed approaches c.

specific.title: reliability
specific.description: An extent to which repeated observations and/or measurements taken under identical circumstances will yield similar results.

specific.title: repulsion (electrical)
specific.description: The force that pushes 2 like electric charges away from each other.

specific.title: scientific investigation
specific.description: A scientific process of answering a question, exploring an idea or solving a problem, which requires activities such as planning a course of action, collecting data, interpreting data, reaching a conclusion and communicating these activities. Investigations can include practical and/or secondary-source data or information.

specific.title: simultaneity
specific.description: The concept that 2 events that occur at the same for one observer may not appear to do so for another observer, depending on their relative motion.

specific.title: standard deviation
specific.description:
A measure of the variability or spread of a dataset. It gives an indication of the degree to which the individual data values are spread around their mean.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Advanced: For a random variable, the standard deviation is the square root of its variance.

It provides a measure of the spread of the probability density function.

specific.title: standing wave
specific.description: A wave in which the nodes appear to remain stationary, while the antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude.

specific.title: superposition
specific.description: Two or more waves meet at a point, the total displacement of which is equal to the algebraic sum of the displacements of the individual waves.

specific.title: thermionic emission
specific.description: The release of electrons from the surface of a heated metal.

specific.title: time dilation
specific.description: The relativistic effect where time passes at different rates for observers in relative motion.

specific.title: torque
specific.description: The tendency of a force to cause rotation about a point or axis.

specific.title: translational velocity
specific.description: The rate at which an astronomical object changes position in space.

specific.title: transmutation
specific.description: The process by which one chemical element or isotope is converted into another when the number of protons in a nucleus changes.

specific.title: transverse (wave)
specific.description: A wave motion in which all points of the wave oscillate along paths perpendicular to the direction of the wave's movement, e.g. surface ripples on water, seismic S (secondary) waves, and electromagnetic waves like radio and light.

specific.title: trend
specific.description: A general direction or pattern in data or observations that shows how something changes over time or under different conditions.

specific.title: uniform circular motion
specific.description: The movement of an object along a circular path at a constant speed, with its direction continuously changing and causing a centripetal acceleration directed toward the circle's centre.

specific.title: validity
specific.description: The extent to which the processes and resultant data measure what was intended.

specific.title: weak force
specific.description: One of the 4 fundamental forces of nature responsible for processes that change one type of particle into another, particularly within the nuclei of atoms.

specific.title: work
specific.description: The transfer of energy that occurs when an external force is applied to an object, causing it to move in the direction of the force.

specific.title: work function
specific.description: The minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the surface of a material (typically a metal) into a vacuum.
